title: U.S. House · Virginia's 8th District
area: Northern Virginia, including Arlington, Alexandria, Falls Church and parts of Fairfax County.

context.text: Incumbent Don Beyer won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 67.6% of the vote over Mo Seifeldein (17.6%), Adam Dunigan (9.0%), Michael Duffin (3.2%) and Lorena Bruner (2.6%). Tony Sabio advanced from the Republican primary unopposed after it was canceled. Cook Political Report, Decision Desk, Inside Elections and Sabato's Crystal Ball all rate the race Solid/Safe Democratic as of September 22, 2026.

candidates.name: Donald Sternoff Beyer Jr.
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 67.6% of the vote.

summary.text: Don Beyer is the Democratic incumbent seeking a seventh term representing Virginia's 8th District. A longtime Northern Virginia auto-dealership owner, he served as Lieutenant Governor of Virginia and as U.S. Ambassador to Switzerland and Liechtenstein before entering Congress in 2015. He serves on the House Ways and Means Committee and the Joint Economic Committee and campaigns on opposing the Trump administration's tariffs and tax cuts and expanding affordable housing and health coverage.

background.text: Born in 1950 in the Free Territory of Trieste, the son of a U.S. Army officer, and raised in Washington, D.C.
Graduated from Gonzaga College High School in Washington, D.C., and was named a Presidential Scholar; earned a bachelor's degree from Williams College.

Began with a summer job at a car dealership in 1974 and spent four decades building his family's auto business in Northern Virginia, which Wikipedia reports he sold to his brother in 2019. Was a co-founder of the Northern Virginia Technology Council.

Served as Lieutenant Governor of Virginia from 1990 to 1998, with signature work on advocacy for Virginians with disabilities and protections for vulnerable residents during the state's mid-1990s welfare reform; was the Democratic nominee for governor in 1997 and lost to Jim Gilmore.
Spent 14 years as chair of Jobs for Virginia Graduates, a high school dropout-prevention program, and chaired the Virginia Economic Recovery Commission.

Served as U.S. Ambassador to Switzerland and Liechtenstein from 2009 to 2013 after being nominated by President Obama, advocating for stricter sanctions on Iran and working with the Justice Department on Swiss bank-secrecy abuses.
Won the 2014 Democratic primary for the open 8th District seat held by retiring Rep. Jim Moran, then the general election; he has been re-elected five times since.
Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means and the Joint Economic Committee, which he chaired in the 117th Congress (2021-2022).
According to his official biography, he and his wife Megan live in Alexandria, Virginia, and he has four children and two grandchildren.

priorities.text: Opposing the Trump administration's tariffs and tax cuts for high earners.
priorities.quote: I've helped focus counterattacks on Trump's tariffs, tax cuts for the rich, and broader economic record. I will not shy away from challenging this lawless president, or for standing up for federal workers and contractors, immigrants, LGBTQ+ people, and all those who have unjustly come under threat.

priorities.text: Building a more equitable economy, including universal paid leave, gun-violence prevention and climate action.
priorities.quote: creating a more equitable economy, ensuring everyone is treated fairly, supporting workers and guaranteeing them universal paid leave, fighting gun violence, and winning the fight against climate change.

priorities.text: Expanding the Affordable Housing Tax Credit and extending health-care tax credits to lower costs.
priorities.quote: In Congress, I have championed expansion of the Affordable Housing Tax Credit to spur the construction of new homes and bring down housing prices. I've helped pass legislation that would extend health care tax credits that make health coverage more affordable.

positions.summary: Says eliminating tariffs is one of the most effective steps to make life more affordable for Americans.
positions.quote: Eliminating Trump's tariffs is one of the most effective steps we can take to make life affordable for the American people.

positions.summary: Says he has championed expansion of the Affordable Housing Tax Credit in Congress to spur construction of new homes.

Says he helped pass legislation extending health-care tax credits that make coverage more affordable, and opposes legislation that would drive up electricity prices by cutting clean-energy investment.
Lists fighting gun violence and climate change among his priorities, and opposed legislation he said would drive up electricity prices by killing clean-energy investment.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means and the Joint Economic Committee.

candidates.name: Tony Sabio
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed after the primary was canceled.

summary.text: Tony Sabio is the Republican nominee challenging incumbent Don Beyer. A Navy veteran who later worked for the U.S. Secret Service and the CIA, he moved into the private sector and has run before for the Fairfax County School Board. He says he is running on national-security legislation, small-business support, workforce development and reducing political division.

background.text: Born in San Juan, Puerto Rico; Annandale Today reports that his mother is Puerto Rican and his father is Filipino.
Served in the U.S. Navy from 1996 to 2002, according to Ballotpedia, and moved to Northern Virginia after his Navy service.
Went on to work for the U.S. Secret Service and the Central Intelligence Agency, then moved into the private sector; describes himself as a small business owner and national security professional.
Ran for the Providence District seat on the Fairfax County School Board in 2023 and lost to incumbent Karl Frisch, 66.9% to 32.5%.
Ran for chairman of the Fairfax County Republican Committee in 2024 and lost to Katie Gorka.
Launched a campaign to challenge Rep. Beyer in 2025 and was unopposed for the Republican nomination in the August 4, 2026 primary.
Lives in Vienna, Virginia, according to Annandale Today; Ballotpedia lists affiliations with the American Legion, Patriot Guard Riders and The Worthy Ranch.

priorities.text: Introducing legislation on day one covering national security, small business tax relief, workforce apprenticeships and critical-infrastructure protection.
priorities.quote: On day one, I will introduce the Nuclear-Ready Grid Zone Act, Nuclear Workforce Act, Small Business Tax Relief & Growth Act, Workforce Apprenticeship Act, and Small Business Continuity Protection Act.

priorities.text: Staying closely connected to constituents on cost of living, jobs, safety and economic stability.
Reducing political division in Congress and focusing on practical, results-oriented governing.

summary.text: Shelly Arnoldi is the Libertarian Party candidate on the general-election ballot for Virginia's 8th District. A Navy veteran and licensed professional engineer, she describes herself as having more than 27 years of experience managing facilities and construction projects, and she ran for the Virginia House of Delegates in 2025.

background.text: Born in Sheboygan, Wisconsin, and graduated from Sheboygan North High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Marquette University in 1991 on a ROTC scholarship and a graduate degree in environmental engineering from Old Dominion University in 1998.
Served in the U.S. Navy from 1991 to 2001.

Describes herself as a licensed Professional Engineer who has managed major facilities and construction projects for the military, Department of Defense schools, and cultural institutions such as the Smithsonian and the National Gallery of Art; Ballotpedia lists her work as an engineer, federal civilian overseas, and naval officer.
Ran as an independent for Virginia House of Delegates District 16 in 2025, finishing third with 2.8% of the vote behind Paul Krizek (D) and Richard Hayden (R).
Ballotpedia lists affiliations with the Waynewood Recreation Association, Fort Hunt Youth Athletic Association and The American Legion Post 24.

summary.text: Tim Sharman is an independent candidate on the general-election ballot for Virginia's 8th District. Ballotpedia lists no campaign profile or key messages for him; FEC filings show $25,000 in receipts as of June 30, 2026.

researchNotes: Sabio's and Beyer's campaign-website quotes are drawn from Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey and staff-curated profile respectively, which cite and quote their own campaign materials. Arnoldi and Sharman have no public campaign materials found beyond their ballot listing and FEC filings. Biography gaps: no biographical details were found for Sharman, and Sabio's campaign website could not be loaded, so his biography relies on Ballotpedia and news reports.
